svg.aria-label: Fetch, cycle by cycle, and the three redirect tiers
svg.text: Fetch, cycle by cycle, and the three redirect tiers
One fetch group per cycle. The next fetch predictor answers in one cycle. The slower predictors check it two cycles later. Decode and execute check again.
Seven cycles of one fetch group
spans are what each unit does in that cycle
Next fetch predictor entry, as inferred from the fetch group behaviour
PC bits used by the zero bubble tier
full history lookup, compared with the NFP answer
on an L0 miss, target from the L1I line
finds an unpredicted branch, fixes the length
An L0 hit has the next PC ready for cycle 1.
Cycle 3 restarts on the L1 tier or a disagreeing slow predictor.
A hit gives the target, length and end type.
~ len counts up to 16 instructions, cut at the first taken branch.
~ end type is conditional, unconditional, call, return or indirect.
~ Returns take the RAS target and indirects the ITTAGE one.
? way names the L1I way to read, skipping the tag and iTLB.
? mask names the slow predictors this group needs.
Training, all of it KB conjecture
holds whether its set is all strong
its PC matches a trained entry
the tag does not cover the whole PC
fetch jumps to the entry's target
decode finds no branch in the bytes
fetch restarts on the right path
512 sets x 2 ways, PC 10:2 picks the set
○ Code 2 KiB apart lands in the same set.
○ A set holds two branches, so the ways cover 4 KiB.
+ A third branch 2 KiB further on overflows the set.
○ Past 4 KiB a taken branch costs 2 bubbles.
~ About 8192 L1 entries, one target per 24 B of L1I.
? Whether the L1 is a side table is open.
the L0 BTB is the fetch group table itself
test three taken branches exactly 2 KiB apart
no trace cache on the M1
loop buffer source, no timing change
skipped short forward branch bodies deleted
small fetch stack for early returns
PAC bits checked at push and pop
~ inferred: patent reading or author reasoning
